title: Rabbi Naftali Besser: Staying Inspired- "Parashat Beshalah"

chapters.title: Introduction and the Egyptian Empire
chapters.about: Egypt's greatness and the initial positive relationship with Joseph and Yakov

chapters.title: The Shift in Pharaoh's Attitude
chapters.about: The change in policy and how the Egyptians turned against the Jewish people

chapters.title: Discussion on Lashon Hara and Miriam
chapters.about: Rabbi Akiva's teaching on Aaron and Miriam receiving leprosy

chapters.title: Grammatical Analysis of Egyptian Bondage
chapters.about: Examining the words otanu and lanu and the meaning of Egyptian cruelty

chapters.title: Propaganda and Historical Parallels
chapters.about: How Pharaoh used propaganda, comparing it to Hitler and modern antisemitism

chapters.title: Measure for Measure in Egypt
chapters.about: Pharaoh's decree regarding water and the concept of mida keneged mida

chapters.about: Moshe seeing the Jewish people fighting and the lesson of Lashon Hara

summary: Rabbi Besser discusses the transition of the Egyptians from loving the Jewish people to enslaving them, comparing this historical shift to modern propaganda and antisemitism. He examines the language used regarding Egyptian bondage, the concept of measure for measure (mida keneged mida), and the dangers of speaking ill of others within the community.
questions: How did the relationship between Egypt and the Jewish people shift from love and appreciation to severe hatred and slavery?
What is the connection between the language used in the Torah regarding Egyptian bondage and how the Egyptians treated the Jewish people?
How does the concept of measure for measure (mida keneged mida) apply to the decrees of Pharaoh and the actions of the Jewish people?
What warnings does the Torah provide about speaking ill of others, and how does it relate to historical and modern antisemitism?
